case_name: High Court of Delhi and Others v A. K. Mahajan and Others
petitioner: High Court of Delhi and Others
holding: The retrospective amendments were constitutionally valid and did not affect any absolute vested or accrued rights of being considered.
The power and competence of the Legislature to make a valid law and make it retrospectively is recognized, so as to bind even past transactions.

A candidate does not acquire any vested right of selection, but if he is eligible and is otherwise qualified in accordance with the relevant rules and the terms contained in the advertisement, he does acquire a vested right of being considered for selection in accordance with the rules as they existed on the date of advertisement.
The applicable rule would be the one which had been validly brought on the statute book from an anterior date, unless it is set aside as being unconstitutional.
